The rain fell in a steady, rhythmic whisper against the windowpane,
blurring the city lights into smudges of gold and crimson. Inside the small
café, the world felt suspended in a warm, amber glow. The scent of freshly
ground coffee beans mingled with the quiet murmur of conversations and the
soft hiss of the espresso machine.

Eleanor sat by the window, her fingers wrapped around a porcelain cup that
had long since gone cold. She wasn’t drinking anymore; she was watching.
Across the street, a man in a worn trench coat struggled with a stubborn
umbrella, a small, silent comedy playing out against the grey backdrop of
the afternoon. A moment later, a young woman ran to him, laughing, and they
disappeared together into the shelter of a doorway.

Eleanor smiled. It was a small thing, a fleeting act of connection in the
vastness of the city, yet it felt significant. Here, among strangers
seeking refuge from the storm, she was reminded that even on the greyest
days, life pulsed with small, hopeful gestures. She signaled the waiter for
a fresh cup, ready to sit a while longer and simply watch the world go by.
